facts.text: Male house sparrows wear bold black, white and brown markings, while females and young birds are plain pale brown and grey.
facts.quote: Females and young birds are coloured pale brown and grey, and males have brighter black, white, and brown markings.

facts.text: In breeding season, male house sparrows repeat their chirping call rapidly and emphatically, forming a song sometimes called an ecstatic call.
facts.quote: In the breeding season, the male gives this call repetitively, with emphasis and speed, but not much rhythm, forming what is described either as a song or an "ecstatic call" similar to a song.

facts.text: Despite being smaller, female house sparrows dominate at feeders and nests, and will even fight males during the breeding season.
facts.quote: At feeding stations and nests, female house sparrows are dominant despite their smaller size, and they can fight over males in the breeding season.

facts.text: Young house sparrows are fed mostly on insects, especially grasshoppers and crickets, until they are about 15 days old.
facts.quote: Young house sparrows are fed mostly on insects until about 15 days after hatching.

facts.text: The house sparrow has a stout, conical bill strongly built for eating seeds, plus a compact body with a full chest and large rounded head.
facts.quote: The house sparrow is a compact bird with a full chest and a large, rounded head. Its bill is stout and conical with a culmen length of 1.1–1.5 cm (0.43–0.59 in), strongly built as an adaptation for eating seeds.

facts.text: House sparrows sleep with their bill tucked under the scapular feathers and often roost together in trees or shrubs outside the breeding season.
facts.quote: House sparrows sleep with the bill tucked underneath the scapular feathers. Outside of the reproductive season, they often roost communally in trees or shrubs.

facts.text: In temperate farmland, about 90% of the house sparrow's diet is seeds, and where it has a choice it prefers cereals like oats, wheat or maize.
facts.quote: Several studies of the house sparrow in temperate agricultural areas have found the proportion of seeds in its diet to be about 90%. It will eat almost any seeds, but where it has a choice, it prefers cereals: oats, wheat or maize.

facts.text: The house sparrow typically avoids extensive woodlands, grasslands, polar regions and hot, dry deserts far from human development.
facts.quote: Though found in widely varied habitats and climates, it typically avoids extensive woodlands, grasslands, polar regions, and hot, dry deserts far away from human development.

facts.text: House sparrows bathe in dust or water in groups, and scratch their head with a leg over the drooped wing.
facts.quote: Dust or water bathing is common and often occurs in groups. Anting is rare. Head scratching is done with the leg over the drooped wing.

facts.text: Female house sparrows use a trilled chur-chur-r-r-it-it-it-it call to establish dominance over males while displacing them to feed young or incubate eggs.
facts.quote: Aggressive males give a trilled version of their call, transcribed as "chur-chur-r-r-it-it-it-it". This call is also used by females in the breeding season, to establish dominance over males while displacing them to feed young or incubate eggs.
